# SEC-001: Platform app .env files are readable by their owner only

- **Group:** Secrets on disk
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

App and service .env files hold database passwords, API keys and tokens. Platforms rewrite them on every deploy, often as 0644, so any local user or compromised process can read every app's secrets. stackward reads only their mode, never their contents.

## Verify by hand

```sh
find /data/coolify/applications /data/coolify/services /etc/dokploy/applications /etc/dokploy/compose -name '.env*' -perm /044 -ls
```

## How to fix it

chmod 600 the files, and add a systemd timer or path unit that repeats it, because the platform rewrites them on the next deploy.

## What a fix can break

A container that reads the file as a different user than its owner loses access; check the app still starts.

Run `stackward explain SEC-001` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
